subject: Discovery recap: latency & throughput targets (p95) — Finly
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@finly.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up / prod constraints

Thanks for the demo earlier — quick recap from our side and the biggest blockers we mentioned on the call. Appreciate any initial thoughts before we sync on the POC plan.

Key pain points we need to solve:
- Latency: our users expect a streaming experience. Current infra has p95 generation time ~= 420ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) which causes visible lag in the UI. We want to get p95 consistently <= 200ms for token-by-token streaming for interactive flows.
- Throughput / concurrency: peak concurrency is ~500 active users hitting generation endpoints (concurrent streaming sessions). Sustained QPS is ~1200 requests/minute during peak batches.
- Cold-starts & KV-cache: models with large context windows add stall during the first few tokens; need warm cache behavior across bursts.
- Cost: we're currently on a self-hosted cluster running mixed A100s and T4s and spend is unpredictable due to tail latency spikes.

Current stack:
- Front end: single-page app with streaming token rendering.
- Backend: Kubernetes (EKS) with a custom inference service that shards requests to a Triton-based runner + CPU-based pre/post-processing.
- Auth & data: customer data never leaves our VPC; we need encryption and audit logs.

Success criteria for POC (what we will measure):
- Achieve p95 <= 200ms for interactive generation at typical prompt sizes (<=256 tokens) for 95% of traffic.
- Demonstrate stable streaming UX with <50ms inter-token jitter once streaming begins.
- Support 500 concurrent streaming sessions with acceptable degradation (p99 tail latency within 2x baseline).
- Show cost-per-token estimates and projected monthly spend for expected usage.

Next steps we discussed:
- Redwood to propose a POC plan and resource sizing.
- We'll provide representative prompt set and traffic profile (attached: finly-requested-metrics.xlsx).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra team (we can do Fri 2/13 morning PT).

Thanks — happy to clarify anything.

—Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Product, Finly
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Thanks Sarah — great meeting. Below is a concise recap from our side, confirming the pain points and outlining an initial POC approach and next steps. Please let me know if I mischaracterized anything.

Recap of pain points (confirmed):
- p95 latency target: <= 200ms for interactive flows (short prompts <=256 tokens).
- Streaming UX requirement: token-by-token streaming with low inter-token jitter (<50ms).
- Concurrency requirement: support ~500 concurrent streaming sessions; peak QPS ~20 rps (~1200 rpm).
- Cold-start / KV-cache behavior: need warm caching and predictable warmup strategy.
- Security: everything must operate inside the VPC; audit logs and KMS integration required.

Initial POC goals (what Redwood will demonstrate):
1) Performance baseline: run your representative prompt set on a Redwood-managed POC deployment sized to match your concurrency profile and measure p50/p95/p99 for both non-streaming and streaming modes.
2) Streaming stability: demonstrate token-by-token streaming with measured inter-token jitter and end-to-end client-to-render time.
3) Failure modes & fallbacks: show graceful degradation (model variant fallback / queued requests) under load.
4) Cost model: provide per-token and per-session cost projections based on observed throughput.

Technical assumptions / questions for sizing:
- Which model family do you plan to use in the POC? (open-source LlamaX / Mistral / custom finetune)
- Typical prompt length distribution (you mentioned most prompts are 32–128 tokens; confirm % of prompts >256 tokens).
- Do you require strict single-tenant GPUs for the POC, or is a shared-dedicated pool acceptable?

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- You share the prompt set and traffic CSV (we got finly-requested-metrics.xlsx).
- Redwood sends a one-page POC checklist + resource sizing by EOD Friday. (attachment: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf)
- Technical deep-dive with Marissa (Redwood SE) and your infra team — proposed Fri 2/13 9:30am PT.
- Kickoff POC the week of 2/17; 2-week measurement window.

If that aligns, I'll schedule the deep-dive and ship the checklist.

Best,
Aditya Rao

aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@finly.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 20:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up / prod constraints

Adding a few technical clarifications and what we'll need from your infra team to size the POC accurately. I left some items as "required" vs "nice-to-have".

Required for accurate sizing:
- Model family and checkpoint you want us to benchmark (name + size). If you have a custom finetune, a small sample (tar.gz config + weights metadata) helps.
- Traffic shape: concurrent sessions, average session length in tokens, and burst profile (how long do bursts last).
- Client-side streaming implementation: do you use server-sent events (SSE) or websockets? We'll need to validate end-to-end latency measurement approach.
- Ops access: temporary read-only access to a metrics dashboard (Datadog / Prometheus) or exported CSVs for current p95/p99 numbers so we can correlate.

POC technical plan (high-level):
1) Baseline run: run your prompt set against a Redwood POC with same model and measure p50/p95/p99 and inter-token jitter.
2) Batching and KV-cache tuning: we'll test batching strategies and prefix/KV caching to reduce median and tail latency.
3) Scaling test: run a load test to 500 concurrent streaming sessions, measure tail behavior and CPU/GPU utilization.
4) Streaming UX validation: we will instrument from client to renderer to capture render time and per-token gaps.

Measurement artifacts we'll deliver:
- CSV of per-request latencies (p50/p95/p99) for each run.
- Inter-token jitter distribution and example flame graphs.
- Cost projection: per-token and per-session.

Logistics:
- For a POC with 500 concurrent sessions, we'd recommend an initial POC cluster built on 4x A100 80GB (or equivalent) for stable streaming performance; we can size down for cost testing.
- If you need single-tenant GPUs for compliance, mark that as required; it increases cost and may change the sizing.

I've attached the POC checklist so you can see the inputs we'll need. Happy to go deeper on any point in the technical deep-dive.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
